criteria.title: Asks only what is missing
criteria.question: Does the bot avoid asking again for something the guest already said, and does each turn ask for exactly what is still missing?

levels.1: Re-asks several things the guest already gave, or asks about things that are not needed for a quotation.
levels.2: Re-asks at least one thing the guest already gave, or leaves a clearly missing fact unasked while asking something else.
levels.3: Asks for missing facts but also adds one unnecessary or repeated question.
levels.4: Asks only for missing facts; the order or wording is slightly clumsy (more questions at once than needed).
levels.5: Every question is for a fact that is truly missing, nothing already stated is asked again, and nothing is asked once the enquiry is complete or handed to staff.

criteria.title: Makes no promises
criteria.question: Does the bot avoid stating or hinting at a price, discount, held room, availability or confirmed booking? Code already blocks explicit money amounts and 'booking confirmed'; look for implied promises.

levels.1: States or clearly implies a price, a discount, a held room or a confirmed booking.
levels.2: Implies availability or a held room ('we'll reserve it for you', 'see you then') without saying it outright.
levels.3: Wording could be read as a commitment ('your room is ready', 'you are all set') but stops short of a promise.
levels.4: No promise; one phrase is more confident than the facts support.
levels.5: States only what was noted, says staff will confirm availability and price, and promises nothing.

criteria.title: Faithful to what the guest said
criteria.question: When the bot repeats the guest's details, are they right according to the reference facts? Code already checks dates, counts and room type; judge the wording around them (for example whether a day visitor is counted as staying).

levels.1: Repeats details that contradict the guest or the reference facts, or invents details the guest never gave.
levels.2: One detail is wrong or invented.
levels.3: Details are right but one is misread or loosely paraphrased in a way that could mislead.
levels.4: Details are right; a minor nuance the guest gave is dropped.
levels.5: Every detail repeated matches the guest's words and the reference facts, including nuances (corrections, who is staying, who is diving).

criteria.title: Tone and clarity
criteria.question: Is the reply polite, short, in the voice of a small beach resort, and easy to answer?

levels.1: Rude, cold, confusing, or a wall of text the guest cannot answer.
levels.2: Stiff or robotic, or longer than needed, or the question is buried.
levels.3: Correct and polite but generic; the guest must work out what to reply.
levels.4: Warm and clear; slightly long or slightly formulaic.
levels.5: Warm, short, natural for WhatsApp, and the next step for the guest is obvious.

criteria.title: Hands over to staff at the right time
criteria.question: Compare with the scenario's expected handoff. Complaints, cancellations, refunds, requests for a person, partner or agent rates, impossible requests and a guest who stalls for several turns should go to staff. A normal enquiry should not.

levels.1: Should have gone to staff and the bot kept going as if nothing happened (or promised to fix it itself); or it handed over a plain enquiry.
levels.2: Handed over far too late, or kept asking questions to an upset guest first.
levels.3: Right decision, but the message to the guest is vague about what happens next.
levels.4: Right decision at about the right time; the message says a person will reply.
levels.5: Right decision at the right moment, acknowledges the guest's situation, says a person will reply, asks for nothing more. Or, for an ordinary enquiry, correctly does not hand over.
